title: Anchored Quicklane & Swim Window — Compact Sidebar + Workspace Swap Proposal
creator: Marisol Vega
description: Problem: Console navigation is crowded for customers who manage multiple workspaces and routinely switch between dashboards, rollouts, and cost views. Goal: propose a compact ‘Quicklane + Swim Window’ pattern — a slim anchored sidebar with contextual quick lanes (Workspaces, Rollouts, Dashboards, Cost) and a temporary swim window modal that surfaces a focused workspace preview and quick actions without a full route change. Scope: IA mapping, sidebar compact states, swim-window prototypes for 3 key flows (switch workspace, preview rollout status, quick cost snapshot). Out of scope: full permissions UI, backend routing changes (handled by ENG). Success metrics: reduce time-to-switch by 30% in prototype testing, reduce accidental full-route swaps (user-reported) by 50%, no regression on token-cost telemetry flows.
ux_research_findings: In 8 moderated sessions users expressed desire to peek at rollout status without navigating away from metrics (7/8)
Frequent workspace switchers preferred a transient preview over full navigation to preserve context (5/8)
Users worried about discoverability of compact rail states — suggest persistent affordance and tour
acceptance_criteria: Compact sidebar collapsed state shows 4 quick lanes with icons and numeric badges
Swim window opens keyboard-accessible with workspace preview and two primary actions: Switch / Peek Metrics
Prototype shows no more than 2 route changes in a sample task flow during user test
Design tokens match console theming and accessibility contrast standards

final_decisions: Use anchored compact rail (28px) with hover/expand to reveal labels, persistent quick-lane icons for core surfaces
Swim window is a transient overlay (ARIA dialog) that does not alter primary route unless user hits 'Switch'
Cost snapshots default to cached view with explicit live refresh to avoid accidental billing/api hits
risks_and_tradeoffs: Adding swim-window increases surface code complexity and requires careful focus management for keyboard users
Cached cost snapshot reduces live accuracy but avoids billing surprises — tradeoff accepted for first iteration
Compact rail may reduce discoverability; mitigation: onboarding tooltip and keyboard shortcut
